cases.question: What manages memory sharing in shared-memory multiprocessors?

sources.quote: Memory sharing managed by shared OS

cases.question: What address space is shared among processing elements in shared-memory multiprocessors?

sources.quote: Physical address space shared among PEs

cases.question: What is another name for Uniform Memory Access multiprocessors?

sources.quote: Also known as Symmetric Multi-processors (SMPs)

cases.question: How can UMA processors reduce the shared memory bus bottleneck?

sources.quote: Use local caches!

cases.question: According to the supplied notes, bus-based UMA is not practical beyond approximately how many PEs?

sources.quote: Not practical for systems with more than ~32 PEs

cases.review_note: Course-specific approximation, not a universal hardware limit.

cases.question: According to the supplied notes, crossbar alternatives can scale UMA to approximately how many PEs?

sources.quote: Can go up to ~256 PEs

cases.question: How is the NUMA memory address space organized?

sources.quote: Memory address space distributed over many devices

cases.question: According to the notes, how many cycles do remote NC-NUMA accesses take?

sources.quote: slow remote accesses (400 ~ 500 cycles)

cases.question: What do directories track in cache-coherent NUMA?

sources.quote: Directories keep track of “where each block is cached”

cases.question: What kind of interconnects allow high scalability in message-passing multiprocessors?

sources.quote: Mesh/grid interconnects allow high scalability

cases.question: Who controls inter-processor communication in message-passing multiprocessors?

sources.quote: Programmer has a lot of control & responsibility over inter-processor communication

cases.question: When do cache controllers share addresses through the snoop bus?

sources.quote: At every write access, cache controllers share addresses through the snoop bus.

cases.question: After a write-invalidate operation, is the next access to the same invalidated block a hit or a miss?

sources.quote: Write-invalidate protocols:invalidate own copyNext access to same block is a miss!

cases.question: What does ILP stand for in the processor performance notes?

sources.quote: Instruction level parallelism (ILP)

cases.question: In UMA machines, what other name is used for these symmetric systems?

sources.quote: Also known as Symmetric Multi-processors (SMPs)

cases.question: In a shared-memory multiprocessor, who takes care of sharing memory?

sources.quote: Memory sharing managed by shared OS

cases.question: For cache-coherent NUMA, what information about a block does a directory remember?

sources.quote: Directories keep track of “where each block is cached”

cases.question: How do write-invalidate and write-update differ for the next access to the same cached block?
reference_answers: Write-invalidate causes a miss; write-update causes a hit.

sources.quote: Write-invalidate protocols:invalidate own copyNext access to same block is a miss!
Write-update protocols:update own copy (a.k.a. write-broadcast)Next access to same block is a hit

cases.review_note: Must include both protocols and the correct hit/miss relationship; human review required.

cases.question: How does memory ownership differ between shared-memory and message-passing multiprocessors?
reference_answers: Shared-memory processing elements share a physical address space; message-passing processing elements have private memories and OS copies.

sources.quote: Physical address space shared among PEs
No memory sharing →PEs have private memories, OS copies
